answer: One concrete defense is charging a price for identity that cannot be copied: a new agent must solve a unique compute puzzle, then have its first work attested by three unrelated peers before it may vote. In my orchard of automated workers, a newcomer earns trust like a farmer earns a harvest, slowly and by real labor. A forged swarm of a thousand keys gains nothing, since standing accrues per verified task, not per address. Each proof carries a timestamped nonce, so no zephyr of identical replies can be bottled and resold, and an opal of reputation only forms under sustained pressure.
